origin.rerun: scripts/ops/diag_fetch.sh 'journalctl?unit=ict-trader-live&since=<24h ago>&lines=200&grep=database%20is%20locked' (or the vm-diag-request relay with that path); count lines and bursts

what: Identify the holder of the trade_journal.db write lock behind the recurring 'database is locked' bursts on the live trader. MEASURED 2026-11-05 (journalctl via diag relay #23192/#23193, 2026-11-04T00:00Z to 2026-11-05T08:12Z): 59 lines in ~16 bursts of 10 s to 2 min; 55 are signal_audit_logger dual-write failures (a waiter, 3 s busy timeout), 4 are the 02:20Z order_monitor burst. The 08:00:30-08:01:12Z burst stretched an exit pass to 42.0 s and breached EXIT-EVAL INTERVAL (71.2 s). PR for TICK-STAGE2-RECONCILE-OFFTICK bounds the exit thread's exposure (0.25 s telemetry write timeout), but the holder is not known: the relay cannot see sqlite lock owners. Ruled out: ml_decision_shadow (no journal write), db_integrity (mode=ro). Next step: instrument write-transaction hold time in src.units.db.database.Database and the long-lived writers (thread + caller name when a commit follows >1 s after BEGIN), or sample /proc/<pid>/fd + journalctl at a burst via a system-action. | [2026-11-05 lane ML-ENTRY-WATCHDOG-EXIT] SECOND INSTANCE, MEASURED (journalctl via diag_fetch, 16:56:10-16:57:35Z, read_state complete, 463 lines): 'database is locked' on _sweep_package_close_reason_from_trade 16:56:49, venue_protection_snapshot 16:57:01, position_path_history 16:57:07, order_monitor protective-level sync + order_packages update 16:57:21/24, signal_audit_logger 16:57:29. The exit-loop's per-pass order_monitor lines gapped 16:56:15 -> 16:57:29 (74.0 s), which is the 16:58Z 'EXIT-EVAL INTERVAL BREACHED 74.3s' page (process started 16:51:10, so NOT the restart). Holder still unknown. | [2026-11-05 lane MECH-FOLLOWUPS-1105, for Manager 2026-11-05b] TREND EVIDENCE, exit-eval interval vs its 60 s requirement (numbers as reported by the manager's routine; the 16:58Z page is the one already recorded above): 74.3 s BREACH at 16:58Z (attributed above to the 16:56:49-16:57:29Z lock burst); 56.5 s near miss at 20:01Z; 59.0 s near miss at 21:47Z. Three crossings above 56 s in ~5 h, so this is a trend, not a one-off. CHEAP DIAG READ (journalctl via diag_fetch, read_state complete, both windows scanned fully, grep=locked|EXIT-EVAL|slow|timeout|retry): 21:47Z (21:45:30-21:48:30, 1562 lines, 14 matched): SAME SIGNATURE as 16:57Z — 'database is locked' x5 between 21:47:09 and 21:47:25 (signal_audit_logger dual-write x3, _sweep_package_close_reason_from_trade at 21:47:18), and the order_monitor GLD lines are 59 s apart across it (21:46:17 -> 21:47:16), matching the 59.0 s figure. 20:01Z (20:00:00-20:02:30, 592 lines, 10 matched): NO 'database is locked' line in the window, so the 56.5 s near miss is NOT explained by the lock; in that window the tick was serially retrying per-strategy 1h bars from the venue (spy/qqq/tlt/slv/uso_pullback/trend_1h, 'venue has not published this session's 1h bar yet', 6-12 s apart, 20:00:16-20:00:51) right at the hour boundary. HYPOTHESIS ONLY (not established; whether the exit pass shares a thread/resources with that fetch was not checked): broker/venue bar reads at the :00 boundary. Also: the trader PID differs between the two windows (2227932 at 20:01, 2285115 at 21:47), i.e. a restart happened in between. NOT MEASURED: the per-pass exit-eval duration itself (no per-phase timing is logged), the lock holder, and which of the two causes (DB lock vs venue reads) dominates over a full day. SUGGESTED OWNER: the TICK-STAGE2-RECONCILE-OFFTICK lane (it already bounds the exit thread's telemetry write at 0.25 s and owns the exit-loop timing); the lock-holder instrumentation named in Next step above is the way to settle the DB half, and a per-phase timer in the exit pass (DB / broker read / strategy monitor) settles which half dominates. | [2026-11-06 lane MECH-FOLLOWUPS-1105, for Manager 2026-11-05b] 00:02Z BREACH (115.3 s) EXPLAINED, MEASURED (journalctl via diag_fetch, windows scanned complete, read_state complete): the exit-pass log for pkg-bf12adaa61b043f7 runs every ~30 s (:12/:42) all evening; the pass at 23:59:42 was followed by the next at 00:01:38 = 116 s, three scheduled passes (00:00:12, 00:00:42, 00:01:12) missing. In exactly that window the trader logged 11 consecutive 'Error fetching OHLCV: bybit retCode 10006 Too many visits' + 'Rate limit hit, sleeping 15s...' pairs (00:00:05 to 00:01:28). Cause in code: src/exchange/bybit_connector.py:109 get_ohlcv() does a BLOCKING time.sleep(15) inside the caller on a rate-limit error; order_monitor fetches candles=200 per package every pass, so a pass that hits 10006 on several packages sleeps 15 s each. The ~7-10 s spacing of the 11 hits (a single thread would space them >=15 s) shows at least two callers hitting the limit concurrently at the :00 bar boundary. NOT PROVEN: which thread slept (the log carries no thread name), so 'the exit thread slept' is the best fit to the 3 missed passes, not an observation. TWO MECHANISMS, not one (population: the 6 EXIT-EVAL INTERVAL alerts in alerts_ledger.jsonl, read of the last 400 ledger rows, plus 64 'Rate limit hit' lines over 2026-11-05T00:00Z to 2026-11-06T00:07Z, 616,832 journal lines scanned): (1) Bybit 10006 sleeps cluster on bar boundaries (hits at 08:00 x3, 09:00, 16:00 x3, 16:01, 20:00, 20:01 x2, 00:00 x11 ...; 11 in the 00:00 hour vs <=5 in every other hour) and line up with the 08:02 breach (also a lock burst), the 20:01 near miss (56.5 s; NO lock lines in that window) and the 00:02 breach; (2) 'database is locked' bursts line up with 16:58 (74.3 s) and 21:47 (59.0 s; rate-limit only 1 hit at 21:45). The 09:51 breach has no matching rate-limit hit (09:00, 09:30) and was not examined. So the top-of-hour hypothesis is right for the rate-limit mechanism and wrong as a single explanation. Also seen in the 00:00-00:02 window: ib_paper IB gateway circuit breaker OPEN (account_open_positions warnings, 'retrying in 72 s'), whose cost to the loop was not measured. FIX OPTIONS (none shipped; order-path Tier 2, real-money packages are open on bybit_2): A) get_ohlcv stops sleeping in-line: record a per-connector cooldown timestamp and return None immediately while cooling down (callers already treat None as 'no candles this pass'); exit loop never blocks, the exchange-side SL/TP stay at the venue, a package's strategy-managed trail is skipped for that pass. B) stagger/jitter or pre-fetch the bar-boundary candle burst and single-flight through the market_data cache so the exit loop reads cache instead of the API. C) A+B. Recommended: A first (smallest, removes the blocking), then B. Needs before shipping: confirm order_monitor handles candles=None without skipping a protective exit, and a test that a rate-limited get_ohlcv returns within ~1 s. Measurement still missing for the lock half: the holder (see Next step above).
